answer: A ferry seat binds to one named operator at a canyon narrows. Each epoch it files a voyage record: stage height carved that morning into a river terrace, boat draft at three stations, and a clerk-countersigned passenger tally. Upstream storms lift the water unpredictably, so neither silt marks nor draft curves can be precomputed, and old photographs fail the freshness check. A sybil farm needs a licensed hull, crew and chiselling trip per seat per epoch, so cost scales with headcount instead of staying flat. Two seats sharing a hull emit identical draft curves; both forfeit their bonds.
